episodes.tldr: Factory reset? A drug got old rats' livers clearing an Alzheimer's-linked protein again, a start-up says its AI proved a quantum puzzle open since 2008, and a humanoid cleaned a reporter's home.
titles: A drug got old rats' livers clearing an Alzheimer's-linked protein again

episodes.tldr: Level up: an outside review finds AI is now speeding up AI at Anthropic, a drug plus vibration seemed to help flush Alzheimer's-linked proteins in 29 people, and a robot moth grew its own sensor.
titles: An outside review finds Anthropic's AI is improving about twice as fast, mostly thanks to AI
OpenAI says its GPT-6 Cyber found 81 unknown, serious flaws in Firefox
Sydney physicists found a one-bit nudge can send an AI's training somewhere else

episodes.tldr: Early signs: 80,000 blood samples will be searched for the first clues of brain disease, an AI screens questionnaires for Parkinson's, and an hour of nature a week brings half the possible boost.
titles: UK Biobank will search 80,000 stored blood samples for the first protein clues of brain disease
An AI reads long health questionnaires to flag possible Parkinson's sooner
Thirty people with ALS will test a wearable brain interface for communicating at home

episodes.tldr: Self-improvement: Anthropic says AI helping build AI may soon speed up sharply, an early trial fixed a faulty DNA letter in the liver, and six humanoids worked a 24-hour shift.

Pinal, an AI from Westlake University, designs proteins from plain-language descriptions

episodes.tldr: One step at a time: a third blind volunteer got a vision implant, a Huntington's gene therapy got an FDA decision date, and robots climbed Mount Tai's 3,000 steps.

The FDA set a 1 May 2027 decision date for uniQure's Huntington's gene therapy
OpenAI's LifeVal benchmark grades AI on everyday tasks; GPT-6 Astra averages 80.6%
